chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: Benny Carter and Don Redman as multi-instrumentalists
summary: Carter plays trombone, trumpet and piano beautifully and can pick up the alto after months and play perfectly; Redman also played several instruments.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well, was Bennie doing any writing then, Bennie Carter doing any writing?
Oh, sure. Yeah, he was doing writing then when he was with Fletcher. He had started writing then.
Well, he, like Don Redman, was also a great instrumentalist.
Uh-huh.
So what -- Besides playing alto sax, did he do any other things in there?
Don played trumpet. He played trombone.
Don Redman played trumpet?
Yeah, and he played trombone and he played piano.
And what about Bennie Carter? He played trumpet, right?
Yeah, Bennie Carter can play a beautiful trombone, which a lot of people don't know.
Is that so?
Yes, he can. And Don could play tuba.
Uh-huh, and Bennie played --
And he could play --
-- the piano a little bit, too, didn't he?
Oh, a little. You kidding? Bennie played beautiful piano.
He's made many records on trumpet.

I know, I know, and a beautiful sound on trumpet. Trumpet players in California, they say, don't like him today because he don't practice and he come on a record date and pick up the horn, and they had been practicing all day, and Bennie would pick up the horn and play it like he played it yesterday.
Oh, that's amazing.

The same way he does with the saxophone. He might not play the saxophone for two or three months and then pick the alto up and play it like he just laid it down. He's one of the most amazing musicians of our time.
That's right. I agree completely.
That's right.
He was in Fletcher's band then.
What year was that again, just for -- ?
That was 1930.
Ah ha.
1930 I got to hear that band. I was with Zack White at the time and we wasn't doing anything so I got a chance when they played in Cincinnati.
That's when they came to Ohio, huh?
That's right. The same time, the first time I heard Duke was that same year.
